GEN.intro: The first book of the Torah: creation, the fall, and the call of Abraham and his family. It is the Church’s foundation for belief in one Creator, human dignity, sin, and God’s covenant promise.
GEN.author: Traditionally Moses
outline: Creation in six days and the Sabbath
The garden, the fall and the first promise (3:15)
Cain and Abel; the line from Adam to Noah
Noah, the flood and the covenant with creation
Nations, Babel and the line to Abram
The call of Abram; Lot; Melchizedek
Isaac born; the binding of Isaac
Sarah’s death; Isaac and Rebekah; Abraham’s death
Jacob with Laban; Leah and Rachel; the sons
Joseph sold; Judah and Tamar; Potiphar; Pharaoh’s dreams
Jacob in Egypt; blessings; death of Jacob and Joseph

EXO.intro: The liberation from Egypt, the covenant at Sinai and the building of the tabernacle. The Passover and the Law shape Israel’s identity and, for Christians, foreshadow Christ’s Passover and the New Covenant.
EXO.author: Traditionally Moses
outline: Israel oppressed; the birth and flight of Moses
The burning bush; the name of God
The Red Sea and the song of Moses
Manna, water from the rock, Amalek, Jethro
The Book of the Covenant; covenant sealed
Instructions for tabernacle, priesthood and Sabbath
The golden calf; intercession; renewal of the covenant

LEV.intro: Laws of sacrifice, priesthood, ritual purity and holiness, centred on the call “be holy, for I am holy.” Read in the Church as preparing the language of sacrifice, atonement and priesthood fulfilled in Christ.
LEV.author: Traditionally Moses
outline: Ordination of Aaron and his sons
The Holiness Code (including 19:18, love of neighbour)

NUM.intro: Israel’s forty years from Sinai to the plains of Moab: census, rebellion, wandering and preparation to enter the land. It is read by Paul and the Fathers as a figure of the Christian journey.
NUM.author: Traditionally Moses
outline: The census and ordering of the camp
Laws, the Nazirite, the priestly blessing, dedication
Departure; complaints; the spies; refusal to enter
Further laws; Korah’s rebellion; Aaron’s rod
Meribah; the bronze serpent; first victories
New census; Zelophehad’s daughters; Joshua; offerings; vows
Midian; Transjordan tribes; stages of the journey; cities of refuge

DEU.intro: Moses’ farewell addresses on the plains of Moab: a renewal of the covenant and a call to love and obey God. It contains the Shema (6:4–9) and is quoted by Jesus more than any other book against the tempter.
DEU.author: Traditionally Moses
DEU.date: c. 1400–1200 BC (tradition); in its present form perhaps later
outline: Second address: the Great Commandment (6:4–9) and exhortations
Succession of Joshua; Song of Moses; blessing; death of Moses

JOS.intro: The conquest and distribution of the land under Joshua, ending with a covenant renewal at Shechem. Its warfare passages are read by the Fathers spiritually and are difficult for many readers.
JOS.date: Composed in stages; Joshua’s time to later editing
outline: Division of the land; cities of refuge; Levitical cities

JDG.intro: The cycle of sin, oppression, cry for help and deliverance in the generations after Joshua, with judges such as Deborah, Gideon and Samson. The refrain: “there was no king in Israel.”
outline: Incomplete conquest and the cycle of apostasy
Micah’s idol; the Danites; the crime at Gibeah

RUT.intro: A short story of loyalty and providence: the Moabite Ruth joins Naomi’s people and becomes the great-grandmother of David, and so an ancestor of Christ (Matthew 1:5).
outline: Naomi and Ruth return to Bethlehem
Redemption, marriage and the line of David

1SA.intro: Samuel, the first king Saul, and David’s rise. The book shows how God’s choice, not outward appearance, makes a king (16:7).
outline: Hannah, the birth and call of Samuel
The ark captured and returned; Samuel judges
Israel asks for a king; Saul anointed
David among the Philistines; death of Saul

2SA.intro: David’s reign: his rise to the throne in Jerusalem, God’s promise of an everlasting house (7), his sin with Bathsheba and the troubles that followed.
outline: Lament for Saul; David king over Judah, then Israel; Jerusalem
The ark in Jerusalem; the Davidic covenant
Amnon, Absalom’s rebellion and David’s return

1KI.intro: Solomon’s reign and temple, the division of the kingdom, and the ministry of Elijah. Kings are judged by fidelity to the covenant.
outline: Kings of Judah and Israel; Ahab

2KI.intro: The history of the two kingdoms to the fall of Samaria (722 BC) and of Jerusalem (586 BC), with the ministry of Elisha.
outline: Athaliah to the fall of Samaria
The fall of Jerusalem and exile

1CH.intro: A retelling of Israel’s history from Adam to David, centred on Judah, the Temple and the Levites, written after the exile.
outline: Death of Saul; David made king
God’s promise to David; wars; the census
Preparations for the Temple; David’s last words

2CH.intro: The history of Solomon and the kings of Judah, with emphasis on the Temple, worship and the reforms of Hezekiah and Josiah, ending with the decree of Cyrus.
outline: The exile and the decree of Cyrus

EZR.intro: The return from exile under Cyrus, the rebuilding of the Temple, and Ezra’s reform of the community around the Law.
outline: Ezra the scribe and his reforms

NEH.intro: Nehemiah, cupbearer to the Persian king, rebuilds Jerusalem’s walls and leads a renewal of the covenant.
outline: Ezra reads the Law; confession; covenant

TOB.intro: A family story of faithfulness, almsgiving, burial of the dead and prayer, set among the exiles in Nineveh. The angel Raphael guides Tobias; the book is a classic on marriage and trust in providence. Deuterocanonical.
outline: Tobit’s piety and charity in exile
Tobit’s blindness; Sarah’s sorrow; both pray

JDT.intro: A pious widow saves Bethulia by courage and prayer, defeating Holofernes. It is a story about faith under threat, with intentional historical freedom. Deuterocanonical.
outline: Nebuchadnezzar’s campaign and the siege of Bethulia

EST.intro: The story of Esther, the Jewish queen of Persia, and the deliverance of her people from Haman’s plot (the Feast of Purim). The Greek and Latin Bibles include additional prayers and edicts (additions A–F).
outline: Esther’s banquets; Haman’s downfall; the Jews’ edict

JOB.intro: The righteous man Job suffers undeservedly, debates with his friends, and is finally addressed by God from the whirlwind. The book honestly faces the mystery of suffering.

PSA.intro: The Church’s prayer book: 150 songs of praise, lament, thanksgiving, trust and kingship, prayed in the liturgy and the Liturgy of the Hours. Numbering differs between the Hebrew/English and the Vulgate/Douay.
PSA.author: Traditionally David

PRO.intro: Short sayings and instructions on wisdom, prudence and the fear of the Lord, with Lady Wisdom personified. The Fathers read Wisdom as pointing to Christ.
PRO.author: Traditionally Solomon
outline: Instructions of a father; Lady Wisdom
Agur; Lemuel; the woman of strength

ECC.intro: Qoheleth the Teacher reflects on the apparent emptiness (“vanity”) of life under the sun, and concludes with trust in God and obedience to his commands.
ECC.author: Traditionally Solomon
outline: A time for everything; oppression; wealth
Death, enjoyment, and fear of God

SNG.intro: A love poem between a bride and bridegroom, read in the Church as an image of God’s love for Israel, of Christ and the Church, and of the soul’s union with God.
SNG.author: Traditionally Solomon
outline: The wedding procession and the garden

WIS.intro: Written in Greek for Jews in Alexandria, Wisdom praises Wisdom as God’s gift, defends the righteous against persecutors, and reads Israel’s history, especially the Exodus. Deuterocanonical.
WIS.author: Traditionally Solomon
outline: The righteous and the ungodly; immortality
Wisdom in Israel’s history; God’s mercy

SIR.intro: Ben Sira’s long collection of wise instruction on conduct, family, friendship, worship and Wisdom, followed by a praise of the fathers of Israel. Deuterocanonical.
SIR.author: Jesus ben Sira
outline: Wisdom, the fear of the Lord, and daily conduct
Praise of the fathers of Israel
Prayer and the pursuit of Wisdom

ISA.intro: The great prophet of Judah: judgment and consolation, the Servant who suffers for many, and the vision of the nations coming to Zion. Cited in the New Testament more than any other prophet.
ISA.author: Isaiah (and later disciples)
outline: Judgment and hope; Immanuel (7:14); the child (9:6); the shoot of Jesse (11)
Restoration and the new heavens and earth

JER.intro: Jeremiah’s long ministry before and after the fall of Jerusalem: warnings, personal “confessions,” and the promise of a new covenant (31:31–34).
JER.author: Jeremiah and his scribe Baruch
outline: Kings and false prophets; letter to the exiles
Book of Consolation; the new covenant

LAM.intro: Five laments over the destruction of Jerusalem, mixing grief, confession and hope in the Lord’s steadfast mercy (3:22–23).
outline: The man who has seen affliction; hope

BAR.intro: Baruch’s prayer of confession, a poem on Wisdom as the Law, and words of comfort for exiled Jerusalem, with the Letter of Jeremiah. Deuterocanonical.
outline: Confession and prayer of the exiles
Wisdom is the book of God’s commandments

EZK.intro: Ezekiel, priest and prophet among the exiles in Babylon: visions of God’s glory, signs of judgment, the new heart and spirit, the dry bones, and the restored Temple.
outline: The vision of glory and the call
Restoration: the shepherd, the new heart, dry bones
The new Temple and the river of life

DAN.intro: Stories of faithful Jews in Babylon and visions of the kingdoms and the “one like a son of man.” The Catholic canon includes Susanna and Bel and the Dragon (13–14) and the Prayer of Azariah.
outline: Court stories: the furnace, the writing, the lions
Visions: the four beasts, the Son of Man, the seventy weeks, the end

HOS.intro: Hosea’s marriage to an unfaithful wife becomes a living picture of God’s faithful love for unfaithful Israel.
outline: Judgment on Israel and God’s tender love (11)

JOL.intro: A locust plague becomes a call to repentance and the promise that God will pour out his Spirit (cited in Acts 2).
outline: Restoration, the outpouring of the Spirit and the day of the Lord

AMO.intro: A shepherd from Tekoa denounces social injustice and empty worship in Israel, and ends with hope.
outline: Oracles against the nations and Israel

OBA.intro: The shortest Old Testament book: judgment on Edom for its part in Jerusalem’s fall and hope for Israel.

JON.intro: The reluctant prophet who flees God’s call, is swallowed by a great fish, and preaches Nineveh’s repentance. It is about God’s mercy to all; Jesus points to the “sign of Jonah.”

MIC.intro: Micah denounces corrupt leaders and promises a ruler from Bethlehem (5:2). “Do justice, love kindness, walk humbly” (6:8).
outline: Hope: the mountain of the Lord; the ruler from Bethlehem

NAM.intro: Nahum announces the fall of Nineveh, the oppressor, as an act of God’s justice.

HAB.intro: Habakkuk questions God about injustice; the answer, “the righteous shall live by faith” (2:4), is quoted by Paul.

ZEP.intro: A warning of the “day of the Lord” and a promise of a humble remnant who will trust the Lord.

HAG.intro: After the exile, Haggai urges the people to rebuild the Temple, promising that its glory will be greater.
outline: The glory of the new house; Zerubbabel

ZEC.intro: Eight night visions, the coming of a humble king on a donkey (9:9) and the pierced one (12:10), quoted in the Gospels.
outline: Oracles: the king, the shepherd, the day of the Lord

MAL.intro: The last prophet of the Old Testament: criticism of careless worship, the coming messenger, and the day of the Lord (the Church sees Elijah returning in John the Baptist).

1MA.intro: Israel’s struggle against Hellenistic persecution and the Maccabean revolt that restored the Temple (Hanukkah), written in Hebrew style. Deuterocanonical.
outline: Judas Maccabeus and the rededication of the Temple

2MA.intro: An independent account of Judas’ campaigns with stories of martyrdom, resurrection of the dead and prayer for the dead (12:38–46). Deuterocanonical.
outline: Judas Maccabeus; prayer for the dead

MAT.intro: The Gospel written for a Jewish-Christian audience, presenting Jesus as the Messiah and new Moses whose teaching is gathered in five great discourses, and who founds the Church on Peter.
MAT.author: Traditionally Matthew the apostle
outline: Genealogy and infancy: Joseph, the Magi, the flight to Egypt
John’s baptism; Jesus baptised and tempted; call of the first disciples
Opposition grows; the sign of Jonah
Journey to Jerusalem; the Temple; woes to the Pharisees
Discourse on the end; parables of readiness and judgment

MRK.intro: The shortest and probably earliest Gospel: swift, vivid, centred on Jesus’ identity as Son of God and the way of the cross. Tradition connects it with Mark, the companion of Peter.
MRK.author: Traditionally Mark, companion of Peter
outline: John and the baptism and temptation of Jesus
Beginnings in Galilee: calling, healings, controversy
Mission of the Twelve; loaves; the leaven
The way: Peter’s confession; three passion predictions; teaching on discipleship
The empty tomb and the appearances (the longer ending, 16:9–20, is canonical)

LUK.intro: A carefully ordered account by Luke the physician and companion of Paul, with the infancy narratives, parables of mercy (the Prodigal Son, the Good Samaritan), and a focus on prayer, the poor and the Holy Spirit.
LUK.author: Traditionally Luke, companion of Paul
outline: Prologue and infancy: Annunciation, Visitation, Nativity, the Temple
The journey to Jerusalem: parables and teaching

JHN.intro: The “spiritual” Gospel by the beloved disciple: the Word made flesh, seven signs, “I am” sayings, the Last Supper discourse and the Resurrection. John 6 is the Bread of Life discourse.
JHN.author: Traditionally John the apostle
outline: Testimony of John; the first signs; Nicodemus; the Samaritan woman
Healing at the pool; bread of life
Feast of Tabernacles; the light of the world; the good shepherd
Last Supper: washing feet, the farewell discourse, the priestly prayer
Resurrection appearances and the purpose of the book

ACT.intro: Luke’s second volume: the Spirit-filled growth of the Church from Jerusalem to Rome, through Peter’s and Paul’s ministries.
ACT.author: Luke
outline: The Church in Jerusalem; first persecution
Saul’s conversion; Cornelius; Antioch; Peter’s arrest
Paul’s first journey; the Council of Jerusalem
Arrest, trials in Jerusalem and Caesarea

ROM.intro: Paul’s most systematic letter: all humanity needs God’s righteousness, received through faith in Christ; the Spirit; Israel’s place in God’s plan; and life in the Church.
ROM.author: Paul
outline: Justification through Christ; Abraham; Adam and Christ
Baptism, the law, life in the Spirit

1CO.intro: Paul answers questions and scandals in the church of Corinth: divisions, immorality, marriage, food offered to idols, the Eucharist, spiritual gifts, charity (13) and the Resurrection.
1CO.author: Paul
outline: Food offered to idols; Paul’s example
Order in worship; the Lord’s Supper
Spiritual gifts; the hymn to love (13)

2CO.intro: A personal letter: Paul defends his apostolic ministry, speaks of reconciliation, the collection for Jerusalem and the strength found in weakness.
2CO.author: Paul
outline: Greeting; Paul’s plans and the painful visit
The ministry of the new covenant and reconciliation

GAL.intro: Paul defends the gospel of grace against those who required Gentile converts to keep the Law: justified by faith in Christ, free in the Spirit.
GAL.author: Paul
outline: Faith, the promise to Abraham, sons and heirs
Freedom, the Spirit and the fruits of the Spirit

EPH.intro: A letter on God’s plan to unite all things in Christ and on the Church as his body, with practical instruction for Christian life and the armour of God.
EPH.author: Paul (or a disciple in his tradition)
outline: God’s plan in Christ; the Church
Unity, the new life, marriage and household

PHP.intro: A warm letter of joy from prison, with the great hymn to Christ’s self-emptying (2:6–11) and Paul’s teaching to rejoice in the Lord.
PHP.author: Paul
outline: Unity and the hymn of Christ

COL.intro: Paul answers a false teaching by proclaiming the supremacy of Christ over all creation (1:15–20) and calling Christians to live as people raised with him.
COL.author: Paul (or a close disciple)
outline: Against false teaching; raised with Christ

1TH.intro: Probably Paul’s earliest letter: thanks and encouragement to a young church, with teaching on holiness and on the coming of the Lord.
1TH.author: Paul
outline: Thanksgiving and Paul’s relationship with the church

2TH.intro: A short follow-up correcting confusion about “the day of the Lord” and urging steadfastness and work.
2TH.author: Paul
outline: Prayer and the duty to work

1TI.intro: A pastoral letter to Timothy about sound teaching, worship, the qualities of bishops, deacons and widows, and the care of the community.
1TI.author: Paul (or in his name)
outline: Prayer and worship; overseers and deacons

2TI.intro: Paul’s last letter, a charge to Timothy to guard the gospel and endure hardship; it contains “All scripture is inspired by God” (3:16).
2TI.author: Paul (or in his name)
outline: Encouragement to Timothy; endure with Christ
False teachers; the Scriptures; preach the word

TIT.intro: A pastoral letter on appointing elders in Crete, sound teaching and good works as the fruit of grace.
TIT.author: Paul (or in his name)
outline: Teaching for different groups; grace has appeared

PHM.intro: A short personal letter asking Philemon to welcome back his runaway slave Onesimus “no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother.”
PHM.author: Paul

HEB.intro: A sermon on the superiority of Christ, the great high priest, to angels, Moses and the Levitical priesthood, with a call to faith and perseverance (chapter 11 on the heroes of faith). The Church has long received it as inspired; its authorship is uncertain.
HEB.author: Unknown (Pauline tradition)
outline: The Son greater than the angels
Christ the high priest, after Melchizedek
The new covenant and the one sacrifice

JAS.intro: A practical letter on living the faith: patience in trials, controlling the tongue, care for the poor, and faith shown in works (2:14–26). It mentions anointing the sick (5:14–15).
JAS.author: James
outline: Trials, wisdom and doing the word

1PE.intro: Written to Christians facing hostility: a call to holiness and hope, grounded in baptism and Christ’s suffering.
1PE.author: Peter (or in his name)
outline: Living among unbelievers; wives and husbands

2PE.intro: A farewell letter warning against false teachers and affirming the apostolic witness and the Lord’s coming; it mentions Paul’s letters among the Scriptures (3:15–16).
2PE.author: Peter (or in his name)

1JN.intro: Short reflections on walking in the light, loving one another, and abiding in God who is love.
1JN.author: John
outline: Testing spirits; God is love; faith and life

2JN.intro: A brief letter to “the elect lady” urging love and truth and warning against deceivers.
2JN.author: John

3JN.intro: A personal letter commending hospitality to travelling missionaries.
3JN.author: John

JUD.intro: A short urgent letter to “contend for the faith” against false teachers.
JUD.author: Jude

REV.intro: A prophetic vision of Christ’s victory over evil, written in symbolic language to encourage persecuted Christians; the Church reads it with the Liturgy, the Lamb and the new Jerusalem.
REV.author: John
outline: Vision of Christ and the seven letters
The woman, the dragon and the beasts; the Lamb on Zion
The fall of Babylon; the wedding of the Lamb
The new heaven, new earth and new Jerusalem
